Pool Excavation

Digging the hole, and getting the spoil off a block with no room

Pool excavation on residential blocks, where the dig itself is rarely the difficult part. What decides the job is whether a machine can reach the backyard, what the ground turns into at depth, and where several truck loads of spoil are supposed to go on a property with a house already on it.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Pool set out

    Who You, through your pool builder or surveyor

    Position, dimensions and depth. We dig to the set out, we do not create it.

  2. 02

    Approval

    Who You or your certifier

    Pools have their own approval requirements, and so do the fences that go around them.

  3. 03

    Access route confirmed

    Who Both of us

    How the machine gets in and how the spoil gets out. On many blocks this is the whole job.

  4. 04

    Service and stormwater location

    Who Max, with a locator

    Sewer lines in particular. Finding one at depth in a backyard is an expensive surprise.

  5. 05

    Protection of what stays

    Who Max

    Driveways, paths, lawns, fences and the neighbour’s side. Access damage is the most common complaint on a pool dig and most of it is avoidable.

  6. 06

    Rock expectation

    Who Both of us

    If the block is on sandstone, the rate for rock is agreed before we start.

The detail

What actually decides a pool excavation price

  • Whether a machine can reach the yard. A side access of under a metre, a steep driveway or a block with no gate all change the machine, the hours and sometimes the method entirely.
  • Where the spoil goes. A pool generates a lot of material, and most backyards have nowhere to put it. It leaves as it is dug, which means truck access as well as machine access.
  • What the ground becomes at depth. A dig that starts in soil and finishes in sandstone is two jobs. The rate for rock is agreed before we start.
  • What is in the way underground. Sewer and stormwater lines run through backyards and are located before the machine does.
  • What has to survive. Driveways, paths, lawns and fences along the access route. Protecting them is cheaper than reinstating them.
  • Whether anything has to come out first. A shed, a slab, a tree or an old pool, each of which is its own scope.

Removing an existing pool is a different job

The shell comes out, the hole is backfilled in layers and compacted. A pool void that was simply filled is where a future slab finds a soft spot.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Can you get a machine into my backyard?
Usually, but what size machine decides the programme. We will look at the side access, the driveway and the gate before quoting, because a block that only takes a mini excavator is a longer job than one that takes a midi.
Where does the spoil go?
Off site as it is generated, because most backyards have nowhere to stockpile it. That means truck access matters as much as machine access, and it is part of what we assess on the visit.
What if we hit rock?
The rate is agreed before we start, so you are not exposed to a surprise. On the coastal side of Sydney, assume sandstone is possible and plan for it rather than hoping.
Will my driveway survive?
With protection in place, usually. Without it, often not. Protecting the access route is part of the scope and it is far cheaper than replacing a driveway.
Do you do the pool itself?
No. We dig the hole to your pool builder’s set out and remove the spoil. The shell, the plumbing, the electrical and the fencing are theirs.
